about: One card per case: where its fault comes from, what it breaks, how it was adapted, when it does not trigger, how it was certified, and how it relates to other cases. Search records: fault_real_cases.json (stage one) and pipeline_fault_real_cases.json (pipeline).

fault_origins.real_reproduction: the original project's faulty and fixed versions, run and reproduced; no case is of this kind
fault_origins.real_adaptation: a specific public instance (an issue, a thread, a pull request) shows the same mechanism; the author constructed the case in this benchmark's code, and the card says what was kept and what changed
fault_origins.controlled_synthetic: constructed by the author from a fault class, with no specific public instance of its mechanism; grounding, if any, is literature, discussion or documentation

candidate_origins.agent: a repair an LLM agent wrote
candidate_origins.human: a version or contract case the author wrote
candidate_origins.program_transform: a candidate made from another by a program, such as removing evidence
candidate_origins.note: Recorded per candidate when candidates are generated, apart from the origin of the fault.

timeline: Every case was constructed before public instances were searched for: stage one on 2026-10-14, the pipeline cases on 2026-10-22. No case was taken from an issue; a real_adaptation case shares its mechanism with one.
rules: Verifiers are developed on pipeline versions with split development and on stage-one cases only. Contract cases are certification material for the hidden tests and are never used to develop a verifier, since some repeat or resemble test cases.

The two faults of a task count as independent cases only through independent sources; pair says what a test case can show. Cases that differ only by dataset, seed, variable name or initial value are not independent.
Counts are not added across families where cases are related: stage one's 17 faults and the pipeline's faults are reported apart, with the relations the cards name.
A case violating a requirement is reported as that; whether it harms performance is measured, not assumed.

A certification is tied to the contract version, the family hash and the commit it ran on; it shows that the checks agree with the cases, and independence rests on the process: hidden tests the verifier never reads, labels frozen before verifier development.

cases.summary: The wrapper reads the patches at its own positions instead of at the indices it kept, so training takes patches from hospital 1, leaves out as many of the last training hospital's, and pairs most patches with another patch's label.
cases.mechanism: Positions in the filtered index space are used to index the unfiltered dataset.
cases.adaptation: In gemnet_pytorch #4 a validation sampler over a Subset yielded the subset's positions while the DataLoader held the full dataset, so validation read training rows. Here the training wrapper reads the base dataset at its own positions while its labels come from the kept list, so training reads held-out patches with other patches' labels. Kept: the index-space confusion. Changed: training instead of validation, and labels that no longer follow the images.
cases.triggers: Whenever patches the filter drops precede the last kept patches in the base order; in slide order (hospitals 0, 1, 3, 4) all 1,977 hospital-1 patches are read and as many of hospital 4's are left out.
cases.does_not_trigger: If every dropped patch came after every kept one (the mirror's combined index order puts hospital 1 last), positions and kept indices coincide and the fault does nothing; the harness orders by slide for this reason.

related.relation: same consequence (a held-out hospital in training), another mechanism
contract case: the same index confusion with matching labels

cases.pair: Independent sources (gemnet_pytorch #4; the forum's concatenated datasets); both break the correspondence of samples and labels in a filtering wrapper. Supports generalization to a new case of that class.

cases.summary: The wrapper keeps the training hospitals' patches but not their labels, so the right patches are trained on with the labels of other patches.
cases.mechanism: A label list kept apart from the images no longer corresponds to them.
cases.adaptation: In the forum case images and labels were separate datasets that fell out of step through concatenation; here the wrapper filters the images but keeps the unfiltered label list. Kept: parallel lists out of step. Changed: the trigger, a missing filter instead of a concatenation.
cases.triggers: From the first kept patch whose position differs from its index; on Camelyon17 in slide order the 3,533 hospital-0 patches are a prefix and keep their labels, the rest do not (62% of the loss's targets match).
cases.does_not_trigger: If the kept patches were a prefix of the base dataset.
cases.pair: Independent sources (gemnet_pytorch #4; the forum's concatenated datasets); both break the correspondence of samples and labels in a filtering wrapper. Supports generalization to a new case of that class.

cases.summary: The loader samples the kept indices from all the patches with a SubsetRandomSampler: the same patches and labels, in another order.
cases.run: the same patches and labels in another order: a different run

cases.summary: Every epoch seeds torch's global generator and the loader shuffles with it: the same patches and labels, in another order than the healthy project's and subset_random_sampler's.
cases.run: the same patches and labels in another order than the healthy project's and subset_random_sampler's: a different run

cases.summary: A restart rebuilds the schedule instead of restoring it. The cosine is computed step by step from the current rate, so the epoch after the restart still has the right rate, and the later epochs follow a new cosine from it and decay too slowly.
cases.mechanism: On a restart the learning-rate schedule is rebuilt instead of restored.
cases.adaptation: In ultralytics/yolov3 a LambdaLR rebuilt with last_epoch=-1 reset the learning rate on resume. Here a CosineAnnealingLR, computed step by step from the current rate, is rebuilt: the restored optimizer keeps the next epoch's rate right, and later epochs follow a new cosine from it. Kept: schedule state not restored. Changed: the schedule, so the symptom comes an epoch later instead of at once.
cases.triggers: A restart followed by at least two epochs: three epochs stopped after the first train the third at 5.625e-05 instead of 2.5e-05.
cases.does_not_trigger: Two-epoch runs, runs stopped after the second of three epochs, and runs that are never stopped.
cases.pair: Independent sources (ultralytics/yolov3; the forum's empty Adam state); the state lost differs (schedule, optimizer). Supports generalization to a new case of state lost on a restart.

cases.summary: A restart rebuilds the optimizer instead of restoring it: AdamW's moments start again from zero and the learning rate from 1e-4.
cases.mechanism: On a restart AdamW starts again with empty moments.
cases.adaptation: In the forum case the checkpoint held the optimizer's initial, empty state; here the optimizer is rebuilt and its state not loaded, and its learning rate starts again from 1e-4, since restoring the schedule does not set it. Kept: resuming with zero moments. Changed: how the state was lost, and a learning-rate jump besides.
cases.triggers: Any restart: the first epoch after it trains at 1e-4 instead of the restored rate, with fresh moments.
cases.pair: Independent sources (ultralytics/yolov3; the forum's empty Adam state); the state lost differs (schedule, optimizer). Supports generalization to a new case of state lost on a restart.

cases.summary: The model, the optimizer, the schedule and the progress are four checkpoints; the progress is written last and resumed from only when it is there.
cases.run: a correct resume cannot differ: the same run

cases.summary: Every epoch writes a checkpoint named after it, and a restart resumes from the latest one there is.
cases.run: a correct resume cannot differ: the same run

cases.summary: The run delivers the weights of its last epoch instead of the best checkpoint; they are the same whenever the last epoch is the best.
cases.grounding: documentation: Keras EarlyStopping keeps the last weights unless restore_best_weights, Lightning tests the current weights unless ckpt_path='best'
cases.mechanism: The weights delivered are the last epoch's, not the best checkpoint's.
cases.triggers: When an epoch before the last has the highest validation accuracy.
cases.does_not_trigger: Whenever the last epoch is the best, which short runs with a decaying schedule often have; the delivered weights then are the correct ones.

gpu_check.observed: The best epoch of this run was the last, so the delivered weights are the healthy run's: the fault did not trigger.

cases.pair: Independent sources (only documentation for A; RF-DETR and LION for B); both choose the best checkpoint wrongly, by different triggers. Supports generalization within best-checkpoint selection, not to a new mechanism.

cases.summary: A restart restores the epoch but not the best accuracy so far, so the first epoch after the restart replaces the best checkpoint even when an earlier epoch was better. Like last_epoch_delivered it chooses the best checkpoint wrongly, by another trigger: a delivery that is not consistent across a restart.

cases.source: GitHub issue roboflow/rf-detr #969, fixed by pull request #973

cases.mechanism: The best-model selection state is lost on a restart, so a worse epoch after it replaces the best checkpoint.
cases.adaptation: In RF-DETR #969 (fixed by #973) a Lightning callback's best EMA metric was never saved, reset to 0.0 on resume, and the first validation after it overwrote checkpoint_best_ema.pth; LION #213 lost the best validation loss the same way. Here a plain loop's best validation accuracy is not restored from the last checkpoint and starts again at -1. Kept: selection state lost across a restart. Changed: framework, metric (accuracy instead of EMA or loss) and initial value.
cases.timeline: Constructed before either source was found; it shares their mechanism and was not taken from them.
cases.triggers: A restart after which the first epoch is worse than an earlier one.
cases.does_not_trigger: Runs that are never stopped, and restarts after which no epoch is worse than the best before it.

related.relation: contract case: the opposite wrong repair, never taking a new best after a restart

gpu_check.observed: The best epoch of this run was the last, so the delivered weights are the healthy run's: the fault did not trigger.

cases.pair: Independent sources (only documentation for A; RF-DETR and LION for B); both choose the best checkpoint wrongly, by different triggers. Supports generalization within best-checkpoint selection, not to a new mechanism.

cases.summary: The run delivers a freshly built model, the pretrained network with an untrained head, instead of the best checkpoint: a control any metric gate catches.
cases.mechanism: A freshly built model, the pretrained network with an untrained head, is delivered.
cases.triggers: Always; a metric gate catches it.

cases.summary: The checkpoint keeps every epoch's validation accuracy, and an epoch is written as the best when it is the earliest with the highest accuracy so far.
A restart measures the best checkpoint on the validation patches again instead of reading its accuracy from the checkpoint.
The optimizer is built before the head is replaced, so the new head is never updated.
cases.adaptation: The forum case replaced one layer's weight Parameter after the optimizer was built; here the whole classification head is replaced after the optimizer is built.
cases.boundaries: Triggers from the first step whenever the head is replaced after building the optimizer; silent in metrics when the backbone alone separates the classes.
